strategy.summary: Two causes. test/money.test.js fails because commit 26dcac5 ("Show prices with their currency code") changed formatPrice on purpose to `12.50 USD` (CHANGELOG 1.1.0), so the test is out of date and gets updated. test/shipping.test.js fails because commit 28e7c8e ("Move the shipping rates into a table") made shippingFor use `subtotal > over`, so goods of exactly $50.00 are now charged 499 cents. That goes against FREE_SHIPPING_FROM's own doc ("this much or more ship free") and 1.0.0 behaviour. It's an application regression, so the assertion stays and is marked expected-to-fail, and a defect gets recorded.
inScope: Updating the formatPrice expectation to the documented currency-code format
Keeping the $50 free-shipping boundary assertion as an expected failure and reporting the regression
outOfScope: Fixing src/shipping.js (application code; reported as a defect instead)
assumptions: CHANGELOG 1.1.0 is the intended formatPrice format (`12.50 USD`, currency as second argument, USD default)
Free shipping starts at exactly FREE_SHIPPING_FROM (5000 cents) inclusive, per its doc comment in src/shipping.js and the 1.0.0 behaviour the test was written against

defects.title: Goods costing exactly $50.00 are charged $4.99 shipping instead of shipping free
defects.description: AC3: orders whose goods cost FREE_SHIPPING_FROM (5000 cents) or more should ship free, as the constant's doc says and as 1.0.0 did. Commit 28e7c8e ("Move the shipping rates into a table") changed shippingFor to `RATES.filter((b) => subtotal > b.over)`, so the { over: 5000, rate: 0 } band applies only above 5000. shippingFor(5000) now returns 499, and orderTotal charges $4.99 shipping on a $50.00 order. A likely fix is `>=` with the first band at over 0 (or set the free band's threshold to 4999).
defects.evidence: test/shipping.test.js > ships free from $50: AssertionError: expected 499 to be +0
